briefFull: The scheme encourages active parental involvement in their children's education from class 1st to Class 12th, including Intermediate education. This scheme recognizes the pivotal role of mothers in promoting education and fostering equal opportunities and improving academic outcomes.
details: The Government of Andhra Pradesh has launched the “Thalliki Vandanam” scheme, a Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) initiative aimed to empower mothers by providing annual financial assistance of ₹15,000 per child (Including ₹2,000 to School Development). This scheme encourages active parental involvement in their children's education from class 1st to 12th, including Intermediate education. This scheme recognizes the pivotal role of mothers in promoting education and fostering equal opportunities and improving academic outcomes.
benefits: - The mother/guardian is provided financial assistance of ₹15,000 per annum per child, regardless of the number of children, for sending their children to schools/Junior Colleges from classes 1st to 12th (including Intermediate Education).
eligibility:
**Eligibility criteria for the applicant**

1. The applicant should be the mother or recognized guardian of a child studying in classes 1st to 12th (including Intermediate Education).1. Income should not exceed ₹10,000 per month (Rural areas) and ₹12,000 per month (Urban areas)
1. At least one person in the household should possess the rice card.
1. Total Land Holding should be less than 3 acres (wet) / 10 acres (dry/combined).
1. Anyone among the household members if owning a 4-wheeler (except Taxi, Tractor, Auto) is not eligible. 
1. Electricity Consumption should be less than 300 units/month (average annual).
1. Household should not own any municipal property which is 1000 sq.ft and above.
1. Any one among the household members employed in any Central/State Government service/PSU or getting Govt. Pension (post-retirement) are not eligible (sanitation workers are exempted and all employees getting less than ₹10,000 salary per month in rural and less than ₹12,000 per month in urban areas are exempted)
1. Any one paying income tax in household is not eligible
1. The beneficiary should have been included in the household database in the state of AP. In case, the beneficiary is not present in the household database, but the child is present in the database, GSWS Dept. to conduct field verification to establish eligibility and map the beneficiary as per rules.

**Eligibility criteria for the student**

1. Children must be enrolled in recognized schools/Jr. Colleges (Classes 1st–12th).1. The students with 75% attendance in this Academic year will be eligible for extending financial assistance for the subsequent year. If a child discontinues studies or doesn’t meet 75% attendance during the academic year, will not be eligible for benefits for the subsequent year.
1. Orphans and street children admitted through NGOs are eligible for this benefit, subject to confirmation with relevant department.
howToApply:
[Offline]
> **Under the scheme, no individual application is required to be submitted by the student or the mother/guardian.** 

**Step 1:** The School Education Department and the Board of Intermediate Education collect the details of both through the school/Junior College.
**Step 2:** The school/Junior College forwards these details to the concerned department through the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE)/Department Official Portals, and the head of the institution ensures their accuracy. The Welfare Departments share the data of Pre-matric and Post-matric Scholarship students with the GSWS Department.
documentsRequired: - The School Education Department and the Board of Intermediate Education collect the student's details (name, Aadhaar number, gender, caste, sub-caste, date of birth, class, school name and attendance percentage) and the mother's/guardian's details (name, Aadhaar number, age and relationship with the student).

faqs.q: Is the financial assistance limited to 1 child per family?
faqs.a: No. The financial assistance of ₹15,000 per annum is provided per child, regardless of the number of children, to every eligible mother/guardian.

faqs.q: Why is ₹2,000 deducted from the financial assistance?
faqs.a: An amount of ₹2,000 per student is deducted at source from the beneficiary and utilized for the overall development of the Educational Ecosystem in the State. It is credited to the relevant account under the control of the District Collector. The fund is utilized towards schools/Junior College maintenance, hygiene/sanitation and such other items as per the SOP to be worked out by the School Education Department.

faqs.q: Which students are covered under the scheme?
faqs.a: Children studying in classes 1st to 12th (including Intermediate Education) in all Government, Private Aided and Private Unaided schools/Junior Colleges recognized by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, including Residential Schools/Junior Colleges, are covered.

faqs.q: Are students of ITI, Polytechnic or IIIT covered?
faqs.a: No. Students opting for ITI/Polytechnic/IIIT (RGUKT) and other similar courses benefitted by fee reimbursement are not considered under the scheme.

faqs.q: Who receives the payment under the scheme?
faqs.a: The payment is made primarily to the mother's Aadhaar seeded bank account. In case of a single parent, it is made to the father's Aadhaar seeded bank account. If both parents are not available, it is made to the guardian's Aadhaar seeded bank account. In case of orphans, it is made to the District Collectors for onward verification of the orphan and disbursement of the scheme amount.

faqs.q: How is the assistance paid for children admitted under Section 12(1)(C) of the RTE Act, 2009?
faqs.a: The fee fixed by the Government is paid from the financial assistance to the Private Unaided Managements through the Single Nodal Agency (SNA) account of the State Project Director, Samagra Shiksha. The balance amount, if any, is credited to the beneficiary's Aadhaar seeded bank account.

faqs.q: What about students receiving Pre-matric or Post-matric Scholarships?
faqs.a: For SC, ST, BC, Minority, etc. students, the scholarship amount under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) is met by the concerned departments through their Single Nodal Agency (SNA) accounts. Only the balance amount is paid under the Thalliki Vandanam scheme.

faqs.q: What can a mother/guardian do if she is found ineligible?
faqs.a: Ineligible mothers/guardians may approach the Grama Sachivalayam/Ward Secretariat concerned to register their grievances.

faqs.a: No. If anyone among the household members owns a 4-wheeler, the household is not eligible. However, Taxis, Tractors and Autos are exempted.
